summary: Protesters chanted against declining affordability, the Macron government, police violence and poor school conditions.

summary: Donovan James calls Canada's MAID program "evil" after his wife Kristin says she received end-of-life info before even getting an oncology appointment.

title: Macron says limiting Ukraine aid would pave way to 'another war'
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday warned that limiting aid to Ukraine would force Kyiv into an "unjust peace" and risk another war. His statement comes as the United States pushes ahead with efforts to negotiate between Ukraine and Moscow.

title: Guinea opens illegal gold mining trial, 1,200 people arrested
summary: Guinea opened a trial over illegal gold mining on Thursday, November 12, after a crackdown on mineral extraction in the district of Siguiri. There was a ban on "unregulated and illegal" gold mining in the area where the military was subsequently deployed. Security forces have expelled tens of thousands of foreign nationals who had come to work in the region's mines.

title: Toera's homecoming: Madagascar's slain king joins his ancestors after 129 years
summary: In 1897, French colonial troops killed King Toera, ruler of Madagascar's powerful Sakalava kingdom of Menabe, and took his skull to Paris, where it remained hidden in a museum for more than a century. France returned the remains last year, and for the first time since his death, King Toera took his place among his ancestors during the Sakalava people's most sacred ritual.

title: Amnesty criticises South Sudan, UN over failure to heed massacre warnings
summary: Amnesty International said Thursday, November 12, that South Sudan and UN peacekeepers failed to act on warnings of a massacre that ended with more than 200 dead in March. The world's youngest country has been plagued by civil war, poverty, corruption and intercommunal violence since it was formed in 2011. FRANCE 24 spoke to Donatella Rovera, Senior crisis response adviser at Amnesty International.

title: Across Africa: Tunisians drawn into Russia's war with Ukraine
summary: This week: A new report says more than 1,400 Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023. Also, as South Africa races to become Africa's digital gateway, a growing backlash is emerging in Cape Town. Plus music, dance and theatre lit up Abéché as the city's arts festival in Chad drew crowds of young spectators.

title: NGO criticises UN's response to massacre in South Sudan
summary: In tonight's edition: Amnesty International accuses both the government and UN peacekeepers of failing to protect civilians during a massacre in South Sudan that killed over 200 people. Also, more than a thousand people are prosecuted for illegal mining in Guinea. Plus a century after French colonial troops killed him, a Malagasy king has finally come home.

title: Violent clashes near the Sudanese border: At least 65 dead in western Ethiopia
summary: Tom Canetti, our correspondant in Ethiopia, has more.

title: French journalist Christophe Gleizes marks 500 days in Algerian jail
summary: Having been detained for 500 days in an Algerian prison on charges of “glorifying terrorism”, French journalist Christophe Gleizes continues to serve a seven-year sentence despite an intense campaign by his family and friends and the football world. While awaiting a presidential pardon, his supporters are stepping up their media campaign to secure his release. FRANCE 24 spoke with his friend Pierre de la Saussay.

title: Africa: Ghana waste dump poses health, environmental 'crisis'
summary: An acrid haze hung over a sprawling dump in Ghana's capital, Accra, as excavators gouged into mounds of smouldering rubbish. Thin plumes of black smoke curled from burning plastic and rubber, mingling with the rank odour of stagnant lagoon water.

title: Boat capsizes off Senegal's northwest coast, leaving 39 dead
summary: At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years. We try to understand why so many are still willing to put their lives at risk, with our guest Aissata Kane from the International Organization for Migration.

title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing at least 34 people, authorities say
summary: A boat carrying migrants along the hazardous Atlantic Ocean route from West Africa to Europe sank off the coast of Senegal, killed at least 34 people, authorities said Sunday. Only one survivor has so far been found, and "an indeterminate number" are still missing.

title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison
summary: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the deaths of 190 children who were starved to death on his orders in Shakahola Forest. Prosecutors said he had convinced followers to fast to reach heaven before the apocalypse, with some victims beaten, buried alive or dumped in latrines. Twenty-eight accomplices have also been jailed. The case has raised serious questions about the authorities' failure to act on repeated warning signs dating back to 2017, with the death toll from the wider investigation reaching 448 confirmed bodies and around 500 suspected vict

title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison
summary: In tonight's edition: Cult leader Paul Mackenzie is sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murder of 190 children starved ‌to death on his orders. Also, in South Africa, activists warn that new data centres could put added pressure on already strained water and electricity supplies. Plus Senegal continues to celebrate the spirit of sport at the Youth Olympic Games.

title: Nobel laureate Navi Pillay on fighting violence with justice
summary: From the International Criminal Court (ICC) to Africa’s place in the global justice system, the stakes are high. In an exclusive interview with FRANCE 24, Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay discusses international justice. She says it must not be held hostage to political power, as US President Donald Trump targets the ICC. What does this showdown mean for Africa?

title: South Africans eager to vote as local elections put failing services in focus
summary: South Africans voted on Wednesday, November 4, in local elections. Nearly 30 million people were eligible to cast their ballots, with corruption, failing infrastructure and the deterioration of essential services among the key issues shaping the vote. FRANCE 24's correspondent Eunice Masson reports from the ground.

title: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of allowing RSF drone launches from its territory
summary: Sudan accused Ethiopia of allowing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) to launch drones from its territory. What does this allegation reveal about the RSF's military capabilities and foreign backing? FRANCE 24 spoke to Ali Mahmoud Ali, a Sudan researcher at ACLED, the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project, which monitors conflicts worldwide.

title: Ethiopian families fleeing conflict face difficulties with food access
summary: A renewed conflict in Ethiopia has led to the displacement of thousands of civilians. But after years of war in the country and heavy budget cuts, humanitarian organisations have all but left many of the camps for internally displaced people, leaving many without food or health care. FRANCE 24's correspondent Tom Canetti reports.

title: South Africans vote in key municipal elections
summary: In tonight's edition: South Africa's ruling ANC party faces a crucial test as millions vote to elect municipal governments. Also, Ethiopia has expelled six Sudanese diplomats amid accusations it's allowing the paramilitary RSF to launch drone strikes from its territory. Plus an ongoing humanitarian crisis deepens in Ethiopia, where renewed fighting has displaced thousands.

title: What we know about China's military exercises around Taiwan
summary: China has been carrying out major military drills around Taiwan since early November. But contrary to some claims on social media, Beijing's armed forces have not actually implemented a blockade on the island; they just simulated it.

title: Crossing Afghanistan along the 'highway of death'
summary: Highway 1, or the Ring Road, connects Afghanistan's major cities. After September 11, 2001, it became a hotspot for crime and fighting, particularly between the capital Kabul and Kandahar, the Taliban's birthplace. People taking it had to navigate extortions, kidnappings and suicide bombings. What has become of the road after the US-led war and five years of Taliban rule? Our former Afghanistan correspondent Claire Billet and photojournalist Sandra Calligaro returned to the country to find out.

title: Myanmar: Junta carries out double-tap airstrikes targeting civilians
summary: Numerous civilian casualties have been documented in Rakhine State amid a renewed military offensive by the junta to regain control of the area. Available evidence suggests that military aircraft are deliberately targeting civilian sites and carrying out double-tap strikes.

title: El Niño fuels climate disasters: The high price of inaction
summary: 2026 is set to be one of the hottest years on record, with El Niño worsening the impact of extreme weather events. With COP31 underway in Turkey, FRANCE 24 speaks with the UNDP's climate boss about the cost of waiting in a warmer world, and with one of the student activists from Pacific Island nations who took their climate fight to the UN's highest court, and won.

title: Undone by a honey trap? Nvidia's Jensen Huang at heart of China spy scandal
summary: It turns out that the new masters of the universe are human – all too human. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with Singapore-based Chinese tech CEO Alice Huang, who is no relation. She's under scrutiny over the purchase of Nvidia state-of-the-art chips that may have been smuggled back to the mainland illegally.

title: AI, affair and espionage: Why is Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang under scrutiny?
summary: Nvidia chief and tech titan Jensen Huang was in the spotlight on Monday after acknowledging an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence, a claim Beijing denied.

title: Myanmar: Civilians under fire from military junta
summary: More than five years after the military coup, the junta launched a new offensive in September to retake Rakhine State, intensifying airstrikes against civilians and employing double-tap strikes.

title: Hong Kong activist jailed for 10 more years for collusion with foreign forces
summary: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 more years in jail on Thursday for colluding with foreign powers, the second time he has been penalised under the city's national security law. Hong, 30, is one of the most globally recognised faces of Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement and has already spent almost six years behind bars. He is now not due for release until late 2036.

title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong gets 10 more years in jail for foreign collusion
summary: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 more years in prison on Thursday for colluding with foreign powers, a court summary said. Wong, 30, pleaded guilty in September to seeking foreign sanctions against Hong Kong and China under Beijing’s national security law, having spent nearly six years imprisoned.

title: South Korea to deploy military mission to keep Strait of Hormuz open
summary: South Korea will deploy maritime patrol aircraft and an explosive ordnance disposal team near the Strait of Hormuz to help keep the waterway open, its defence ministry said Thursday. Seoul said it would protect commercial shipping and energy supplies while ruling out military intervention in the ongoing US-Iran war.

title: How Chinese AI is censoring the controversy around Mbappé’s Chairman Mao comments
summary: Footballer Kylian Mbappé sparked a wave of condemnation across China when he implied that Chinese leader Mao Zedong was a dictator. In China, information about this controversy is being censored by Chinese AI chatbots.

title: North Korea rejects US allegations over $6 billion Binance crypto heist
summary: North Korea on Tuesday dismissed US allegations that it was behind a $6 billion cryptocurrency theft from Binance as "absurd rhetoric", accusing Washington of seeking to portray the country as a cybercriminal state and warning that US hostility could affect future diplomatic engagement.

title: Thousands join Indian opposition protest
summary: India’s opposition parties staged major protests in New Delhi on Sunday against Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government and a nationwide voter list review that has fuelled demonstrations since the summer, led by the youth movement Cockroach Janta Party. Eliza Herbert reports.

title: Indian opposition parties stage mega rally seeking election chief’s resignation
summary: Tens of thousands of demonstrators on Sunday joined a protest in New Delhi called by Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and backed by the youth “Cockroach” movement amid tight security. Protesters are demanding the resignation of the country's election chief over voter list revisions that critics say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.

title: Foiled Hindu temple plot exposes rising anti-Indian sentiment in the US
summary: In this edition of Access Asia, we explore why anti-Indian sentiment is rising in the United States in the wake of the foiled plot targeting a Hindu temple in Illinois. We ask the executive director of the Center for the Study of Organized Hate what's behind the trend, and whether the rhetoric coming from the Trump White House is to blame.

title: North Korea tests attack drones as Kim calls for 'absolute superiority'
summary: North Korea has tested attack drones, cruise missiles and rocket launchers at a weapons demonstration, state media reported Friday, as Kim Jong Un called for faster development of military drone and artificial intelligence technology. The tests follow a series of weapons trials and rising tensions with South Korea.

title: The Nvidia affair: Are markets about to fall out of love with AI?
summary: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia exposes the vulnerabilities behind the AI boom. As equities reel in response to his resignation following extramarital affairs, alleged Chinese espionage and a summons to testify before US lawmakers, questions mount over who is really in charge of tech and whether the immense capital riding on it can survive the turmoil.

title: Haitian forces recapture national stadium after two years of gang control
summary: Haitian security forces regained control Thursday, November 12, of the country's main stadium that had been under gang control for two years, forcing the national football team to play elsewhere. The Haitian National Police said in a statement that it had taken "full control" of the venue with the Task Force, a private security group serving the government, after which it left the stadium under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers.

title: 'Devastated wasteland': Haitian security forces regain control of stadium from gangs
summary: Haitian security forces said they have regained control of the country's main stadium, wresting it back from the gangs that have been using it for the past two years. They were assisted by the Task Force, a private security group serving the government. The stadium is now under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers. FRANCE 24's senior reporter Catherine Norris Trent, who has covered Haiti extensively, said re-taking the stadium would be a significant step in an area of the city that had been a "devastated wasteland".

title: Midterms: What does the 'blue tsunami' mean for US media?
summary: This week, FRANCE 24's media show Scoop looks at the impact of the midterm elections in the United States. While the results are being reckoned with by Republicans and celebrated by Democrats, what does it all mean for the press? Some media analysts wonder whether certain outlets, particularly ones accused of being cosy with the Trump administration, will change their tone. Our guest this week is International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert.

title: The scourge of femicide in Mexico: Impunity reigns in state of Morelos
summary: When Claudia Sheinbaum became Mexico's first female president in 2024, she pledged to tackle violence against women. And while femicides have fallen since she took office, the numbers remain alarming, with around 520 murders so far this year. In the small state of Morelos, just outside the capital Mexico City, four female students have been murdered since January, including a Spanish woman on an exchange programme. The state has one of the highest femicide rates in the country.

title: Peruvians flock to see Pope Leo XIV in city he served as bishop
summary: Crowds in Peru's northern city of Chiclayo gathered early on Friday, November 13, ​ahead of ‌Pope Leo's arrival for the centerpiece event of his 12-day South America tour, an outdoor ⁠Mass with the people who called him their bishop for eight years. He declared on November 11 that the country where he served as a missionary for about 20 years was his homeland.

title: Pope Leo XIV meets clerical abuse victims in Peru, says Church must make 'amends'
summary: Pope Leo XIV met six victims of clerical abuse in Peru on Thursday, including people linked to the disbanded group Sodalitium Christianae Vitae. The US-born pontiff also urged the Catholic Church to make amends to survivors and strengthen protections against abuse as he returned to the country where he served as a missionary and bishop for nearly two decades.

title: Haitian police retake national stadium after two years of gang control
summary: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main football stadium Thursday after two years under gang control, with Salvadoran troops taking over security at the venue. El Salvador deployed 2,000 soldiers to Haiti following an ambush that left four of its troops missing.

title: 'Peruvian pope' Leo XIV comes home to a country that shaped his life and faith through 'hardship'
summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Victor Casallo, Director of the Department of Philosophical and Theological Studies at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University. Can a pope shaped by Peru's history of political violence, social inequality and religious activism help a deeply polarised nation heal and rediscover the possibility of dialogue? "We tend to see the other person not as someone who holds a different opinion, but as an enemy." Casallo argues that with Pope Leo, the first American-born pontiff's identity cannot be understood through his Chicago origins alone.
